name: devcorner
description: Connects Claude Code to devcorner, which you sign in to from /mcp: opens and closes a devcorner session with each conversation and moves it to the branch you switch to, registers each subagent as a child session, keeps the session the conversation's own start returned, or, when it never saw that start, the one the conversation's own devcorner calls name, and states it with each status read and a resume or compaction, so devcorner ties the window back to it when that tie drifted, and puts new messages in front of the model while it works, whole, while you see one short toast for each hand-over (who, how many, the first words) and never their text, asking devcorner only when something waits; a tool call never waits on devcorner: its hook asks in the background, and what came is given at the next tool call, as the turn ends or at the next prompt. A conversation's start and each compaction give devcorner's standing instructions in hooks of their own, beside the briefing, so neither cuts the other. When something wakes a waiting session, such as your answer from devcorner, a run dispatched to it, news from an OA it gave (a question to you, its mind's stop, its end, a checkpoint that waits on your go), the end of a run it asked for or its pull request's conflict, an idle conversation starts a turn for it, naming what came, once and only while it is unread. A conversation with no session is woken by your own message to it, and other mail to it is told on a toast. /devcorner:cloud-agent sets up your Claude Code routine for cloud runs in one step, and /devcorner:discuss talks a question waiting on you through in the session you are in, posting nothing until you say so. /devcorner:how-we-work is devcorner's operating model, how to work with it and why for any project, which Claude loads by itself when it plans, files or kicks off work, coordinates work through devcorner or keeps docs current. A quiet line above the prompt, drawn by devcorner itself with no warning sign, is one line of links with nothing to press, its words plain where the terminal draws no links (as macOS Terminal), by the rule Claude Code draws links by: devcorner, linked to the project's home, the window's label, the conversation's name else this machine's name and the project, as MacBook Air 1 (Web), then this conversation's session by its short id, linked to its page, and what waits on you in the project, linked to its inbox, only while something does; it fits the terminal's width, the label cut at a word or left out, never the id; the held request names a 25 s hold; in a repo new to devcorner the line says /dc setup sets it up and /dc hide hides the offer; for the minute after a deploy of devcorner the line says devcorner is updating, and the plugin waits as long as devcorner asked before it asks again; /dc says the project's picture as text (Project home, Active actions and In flight first, then the session's ticket, the paste to copy, your other live sessions, what waits on you by work stream, the newest first, the OA, what is moving, cloud sessions, Next and the code against the last deploy, each under a short lower-case label, then their pages), says which person and machine this is, or asks devcorner something; /dc now says what the session is on and did lately (its ticket, its latest note, its last moves, its open questions and its runs out); when an agent of this conversation writes a paste for you, the transcript says so in one line, /dc paste copies it and /dc pastes lists yours; /dc waits lists what waits on you by work stream; /dc sessions lists your live sessions in every project, each with where it runs (its cloud routine, its conversation's name, this machine), and /dc send <to> <text> sends your own words, typed here, to another conversation or session of yours, in any project, which wakes for them while it is idle; /dc chat [title] opens this window as a window chat in devcorner, where its replies stream and your words typed on the page while it works join the turn under way at its next tool result, marked as yours, and otherwise are typed in here as yours while it is idle, one message at a time, each a turn of its own, in the order said, words sent before a reply you had not read marked as such; the page says what holds a busy window (a command it runs in the foreground, a plan waiting for approval) and can move a foreground Bash command to the background, which ends the turn with the command still running, types the words waiting after a note that says so, and with none waiting tells Claude to carry on; and a slash command you send from the page (a skill, a plugin's command, an MCP prompt, or /compact, /context, /model <name> or /effort <level>) runs here alone, in its place among them, with what it came to on the page, and the page's / list offers this window's own skills, plugin commands and MCP prompts, which the plugin sends devcorner as the chat opens and again once they change; /dc chat off stops it, and /dc continue <chat> continues one in another window; devcorner's page can start a window chat on this machine, or move a chat here: an idle window, or the background launcher /dc launcher on keeps (off stops it), takes the ask and the plugin's own script runs claude --bg in the repo's folder, its own session variables cleared, named by the chat's title and id, and says back how it went; a window chat whose background session Claude Code parked comes back from its page, by Revive or your words there, as the same session with its whole context, the script running claude respawn <id>; /dc chat offers /rename with that name. A window that mirrors a window chat is told, once as its mirroring begins and again after each compaction while it mirrors, that its replies are read in a devcorner chat and to write plain chat prose for it. A turn of that chat that an API failure ends (the usage limit, an overload, a sign-in that failed) shows on the page as failed, with one plain line of what happened and what to do, and for the usage limit when it resets. /dc ask <to> <task> asks one session or conversation of yours to do something, such as running the tests or verifying a change, which wakes it while it is idle, and its answer wakes this window, in whatever turn it comes, within 24 h of the ask. /dc mute <id> [30m] [family] turns a noisy session, a run's sessions, a conversation or all of them down for this window for a while: their messages never wake it and are not handed, and when the mute ends or /dc unmute lifts it one message names how many came; /dc quiet <id> lets them in only at the end of a turn, never waking it; the line above the prompt names what is turned down, and /dc mutes says it with the time left. Your own word, runs' ends, dispatches and answers to what this window asked always come through. A machine signs itself in from Claude Code: /dc login shows a code to approve on devcorner's /device page, or Claude approves that code through its own devcorner connection when asked, as the line above the prompt says while signed out, and the plugin keeps the hook token devcorner makes for this machine in the plugin's own store, never in settings.json; /dc logout revokes it, and /dc machine <name> renames the machine, as its connections page does, warning when another machine of yours has that name. With no token, each session's start and /dc say that delivery is off in the window and how to turn it on, and the plugin's first run on a machine begins /dc login itself. DEVCORNER_TOKEN in the environment still wins. Before a web search, a page fetch or a subagent's spawn, the plugin asks devcorner for your earlier work the agent should read first (a decision with its why, the research behind it) and adds devcorner's one line after the tool's result, or to the end of the subagent's prompt, at most once per item in a context window; the search runs at once beside it, a spawn waits up to 2 s for it, and with no answer the tool runs as it was made. A devcorner worker or a fork gets none, and nothing of the tool's input is stored. When an agent reads, greps or globs Claude Code's own auto-memory folder, the plugin adds devcorner's memories for the repo after the result, once per context window and again when one it was not given appears, and a write or edit there is told, by the plugin itself, the line devcorner gives every session at start on what goes in its memory: what every session should know goes in devcorner's, at the narrowest scope that fits, and what is only true on one machine or in one folder stays out; nothing of the path is sent, and with no answer a read's result is its own. With no token, as in a cloud session, which is never signed in, the plugin adds the Claude account's capacity, when a reading is due, to a devcorner call the session makes anyway. devcorner's subagent tool is answered on the laptop, never on devcorner's server: on a signed-in machine, in a conversation that started, the plugin runs the child with devcorner's local agent, Pi on the workspace's box model in a clone of the checkout, and hands back its answer and its patch. It asks once before it installs the local agent (/dc local-agent install does it too), and asks you before each call where no rule allows the tool, since such a call meets no permission prompt of Claude Code's; in claude -p it refuses unless a rule allows it.
